subject: SummitTech vendor onboarding — payment lanes and split-invoice qualification
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@summittech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procure@summittech.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor onboarding — supplier forms + payment lane question

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're starting SummitTech's onboarding for the Redwood pilot and have a couple of questions on the supplier setup:

- We have two internal cost centers for this engagement (Hardware & Services). We'd like invoices routed to separate GLs; can Redwood support split invoicing (one PO, two invoice lanes) so each lane maps to a different AP code?
- Our standard payment preference is Net45, but for the pilot we may request Net30 on the services line only. Is it possible to have mixed terms on a per-line basis?

I've attached our completed supplier onboarding form and a copy of our W-9. Also attaching a sample PO so you can see how our system handles line-level attributes.

If helpful, we can have our AP team on the thread (cc'd). Looking to get this setup before our first invoice in early November.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Vendor Programs Manager
SummitTech
Attachments: SummitTech_Supplier_Onboarding_Form.pdf (application/pdf), W-9_SummitTech.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@summittech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding — supplier forms + payment lane question

Hi Elena — great to meet you over email.

Short answers up front: yes, we support split invoicing / multiple invoice lanes on a single supplier record, and we can honor mixed net terms at the PO-line level provided the PO includes the correct routing metadata. A couple of clarifying items so we can provision accurately:

1) Do you need Redwood to split a single PDF invoice into two payments, or will you be sending two separate invoice files (one per cost center)?
2) For line-level Net terms (e.g., services = Net30 for pilot, hardware = Net60), we need the PO to include the PO-line 'payment_term' tag or a line-level GL mapping. Without that, our system defaults to the supplier-level Net45.

Operational proposal:
- Default supplier-level term: Net45
- Services line for pilot: Net30 (requires explicit PO-line tag)
- Hardware capital purchases: Net60 (flag at PO-line)

We also offer an early-pay program if you need faster vendor payment: Net15 available at 1.0% early-pay fee, Net7 at 1.8% (applies per invoice lane). If SummitTech wants to enroll, we can add them to the 'expedited remit' lane in our vendor portal.

I'll loop in Karthik from procurement to confirm PO routing and David in finance for the early-pay pricing & final sign-off. In the meantime, here's the vendor portal invite link to complete the remaining onboarding steps: https://redwood.app/vendor-portal/invite?token=abc123

Thanks — cc'ing our procurement and finance leads so we can lock this down before 11/01.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks — quick clarifications:
- We'll send two separate invoice PDFs (one for Hardware, one for Services). That should be the simplest from our ERP side.
- We can add a payment_term tag at the PO-line level; I checked with our ops team and they can include 'payment_term=NET60' on hardware lines and 'payment_term=NET30' on services.

One additional ask: a handful of our hardware procurements are already on extended supplier agreements — could Redwood accept Net60 on certain SKUs while keeping Net45 on standard consumables? Is there any limit to the number of invoice lanes per supplier?

Attaching the PO sample so your team can see the fields we populate in our system. We'll also start the DocuSign for the onboarding packet tomorrow.

Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding — supplier forms + payment lane question

Marissa / Team,

Apologies for the delay — confirmed with Accounting: we can support the proposed structure but need these controls implemented up front. Final approach below (approved):

- Supplier default term: Net45 (applies when PO-line payment_term is absent).
- Line-level override: we will honor PO-line 'payment_term' tags (NET30, NET60). When a PO contains both NET30 and NET60 lines, Redwood will create two payable lanes and map each invoice to the corresponding lane based on PO-line metadata.
- Invoice format: SummitTech should send separate PDFs per lane and include PO number and PO-line item references on each invoice header. This avoids split-file parsing on our side.
- Max lanes: we will permit up to 4 invoice lanes per supplier for now; recommend SummitTech use 2 for simplicity.
- Early-pay: Finance approves an expedited remit offering. Pricing: Net15 @ 1.0% fee; Net7 @ 1.75% fee. Enrollment requires a signed addendum processed via DocuSign.

Action items for SummitTech:
1) Confirm they will send separate PDFs per lane and add PO-line 'payment_term' tags.
2) Complete vendor portal onboarding (link provided by Marissa).
3) Sign the DocuSign addendum if they want early-pay enrollment (https://docusign.com/link/summittech-onboard).

Once SummitTech confirms (1–3), procurement will provision the vendor record and finance will enable the early-pay lane if requested.

David Kim
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
